items.title: Should You Get Paid To Wait Out Vertiv's Learning Curve?
items.summary: Vertiv (VRT) makes the power and cooling systems that keep AI data centers running, and the stock trades about 38% below its 52-week high. Selling a put pays you now for agreeing to buy it lower, and the payment is yours whether or not you own the shares. The catch is what knocked the stock down: Vertiv is learning to ship projects far bigger than it used to.

items.title: Should You Get Paid While Eaton Finishes Its Factories?
items.summary: Eaton (ETN) trades about 15% below its 52-week high and has gained less than the S&P 500 over the past year. It is in the middle of what it calls a record-scale capacity build, and that cost lands before the revenue does. You can be paid now for agreeing to buy the shares much lower, and you keep the payment either way.

items.title: Should You Buy Donaldson Stock While Its Share Count Stops Shrinking?
items.summary: Donaldson (DCI) has gained 9.1% over the past twelve months and still trades about 20% below its 52-week high. The filtration company behind those numbers sells replacement parts into equipment already in service, and the cash from that stream has been steadily shrinking its share count. The shrinking count is the case for buying the pullback. It is also the part that goes quiet in fiscal 2027.

items.title: Vertiv Has Guided Itself Into A Steep Second Half
items.summary: Vertiv (VRT) is up about 88% over the past year, and down nearly 14% over the past three months. The number that should worry a holder sits in the company's own guidance: organic growth of roughly 35% in the third quarter of 2026, against the 18% organic pace it just delivered. Everything about the second half of 2026 turns on that step.
